misconceptions.believed: That T4's exit criterion 3 was partly unmeetable -- that the 60-90% success band 'cannot hold for a player who always writes correct code', and that this was a finding against the criterion. Written into S028's journal, its data twin, the flight board, T4 itself, and reported to the user as one of two things standing between T4 and a clean landing.
misconceptions.revealed_by: Reading criterion 3 and the instrument check side by side before landing, because landing is the moment the comparison is forced. First time M45's lesson was applied deliberately rather than learned again.
misconceptions.corrected_to: The document draws the distinction itself. Criterion 3 asks that 'success rate across A simulated 50-level run' stay inside 60-90%, which is verified and robust: 72% for an improving player across 40/40 seeds, 71% for a plateaued one across 38/40. The instrument check below it is the thing demanding the band hold 'FOR EACH' of four named players, and that is what cannot be satisfied. The finding is real; it was against a different line. Criterion 3 verified, the instrument check recorded as partly unmeetable in T4's table, neither re-cut (N7).
misconceptions.generalisable_lesson: I was reading my own summary rather than the source, which is M45 with the roles reversed: there a board summary hid an unmet criterion, here a summary I wrote invented an unmeetable one. A summary drifts in whichever direction the summariser was worried about -- I had just spent a session on the power-creep hazard and read the next line pessimistically. The fix is the same either way and it is cheap: when a criterion's status matters, quote it.

decisions.decision: earned is a set intersection, never a weighted combination
alternatives: Score the pair and threshold it
Let a strong class lower a gate
decisions.rationale: The trajectory's own words: a gate, never an average. Exit criterion 8 is held by there being no blended number to display, which is cheaper and more durable than reviewing every screen that might show one.

decisions.decision: Every class offers exactly two abilities
alternatives: Let each class offer as many as its theme suggests
decisions.rationale: W8's no-class-outranks-another extended to what they unlock. Unequal counts would make one class better equipped, which is a ranking arriving through the back door.

decisions.decision: A gate counts confident tags above a level rather than averaging mastery
decisions.rationale: An average unlocks by adequacy at everything, which is not the claim being made; and a single mastery figure is the shape criterion 8 exists to prevent, even on one side of the wall.

decisions.decision: abilities.py takes the class as a name, not a FunctionClass
alternatives: Import profiler and take the object
decisions.rationale: Keeps the dependency one-directional and light -- abilities imports mastery, which imports nothing -- and stops the ability layer reaching into how a class was derived.

decisions.decision: No class means no abilities, framed as an invitation
decisions.rationale: Abilities are flavoured by how you write, and that is unknown until a profile exists. A baseline would make 'no class' a class; denying with no explanation would make it a penalty.

decisions.decision: T4 lands with its instrument checks recorded in a table, one partly unmeetable
alternatives: Hold T4 open until Q89 is answered
decisions.rationale: T7's precedent. A trajectory does not land on its instrument checks, and counting an unmet one as met is a mistake this project has paid for twice.
